Q1: What should G4 do when a cancelled job hit its time limit (e.g. `tests-release-and-log-analysis` hitting its 20-minute limit), given that the sweep won't re-run it?
Choices:
A) Keep the non-goal. Defer only when the run would actually be re-run: a cancelled job with no timeout annotation, which the classifier already calls `abandoned`. That case logs `outcome=deferred reason=cancelled_jobs_rerun` next to the existing `infra_rerun_deferred`. A timed-out job is handed back as today. In the #9725 case, G1–G3 then stop the repair on the green head. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Drop the non-goal. Add a new opt-out verdict for timeouts (with its own `CI_*_RERUN_ENABLED`-style switch, default on) to `classify-run`. The sweep then re-runs a final-CI attempt-1 run once when its only non-success jobs timed out, and the hand-back defers on the same verdict, so the two always agree.
C) Drop G4 entirely and rely on G1–G3: the hand-back always dispatches as today, and the gate and repair step skip once `ci/final` turns green.
